"""Professional local operator dashboard for Atlas Commerce."""

import os
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st
from pydantic import ValidationError

from adaptive_commerce.application.dashboard import (
    CandidateRequest, bootstrap_database, candidate_report, get_product_catalog,
    list_region_actions, list_region_cycles, list_regions, persist_cfo_import,
    preview_products, submit_candidate,
)
from adaptive_commerce.application.lifecycle import (
    approve_region, archive_region, pause_region, reject_region, resume_region,
    rollback_region,
)
from adaptive_commerce.application.operator import inject_demo_signal, reset_demo
from adaptive_commerce.application.worker import replay_cycle, run_all_active_regions, run_region_cycle
from adaptive_commerce.domain import RegionState
from adaptive_commerce.integrations.finance import FinanceInputs, read_cfo_export
from adaptive_commerce.integrations.observability import initialize_tracing


def render_dashboard() -> None:
    """Render summary, region controls, recommendations, and audit evidence."""
    st.set_page_config(page_title="Atlas Commerce", page_icon="◈", layout="wide")
    st.markdown("""
    <style>
      .block-container {padding-top: 1.8rem; padding-bottom: 2.5rem; max-width: 1440px;}
      [data-testid="stMetric"] {
        background:var(--secondary-background-color);
        color:var(--text-color);
        border:1px solid rgba(128, 128, 128, .24);
        padding:14px 16px;
        border-radius:12px;
      }
      [data-testid="stMetricLabel"], [data-testid="stMetricLabel"] p,
      [data-testid="stMetricValue"], [data-testid="stMetricDelta"] {
        color:var(--text-color) !important;
      }
      [data-testid="stMetricLabel"] p {font-size:.82rem;opacity:.76;}
      h1 {letter-spacing:-.035em;} .atlas-muted {color:#667085;font-size:.9rem;}
      .atlas-badge {display:inline-block;padding:.2rem .55rem;border-radius:999px;background:#eef4ff;color:#214c9a;font-size:.78rem;}
    </style>
    """, unsafe_allow_html=True)
    path = Path(os.environ.get("ATLAS_DB_PATH", "data/atlas_commerce.db"))
    st.title("Atlas Commerce")
    st.caption("Regional commerce intelligence · Operator workspace")
    flash = st.session_state.pop("flash_success", None)
    if flash:
        st.success(flash)
    try:
        bootstrap_database(path)
    except (OSError, sqlite3.Error, ValidationError, ValueError):
        st.error("The workspace database could not be initialized. Check its path and fixture data.")
        return
    tracing = initialize_tracing()
    st.caption(f"Observability · neatlogs {tracing.status.title()} — {tracing.detail}")
    _integration_status(tracing.status, tracing.detail)
    regions = list_regions(path)
    if not regions:
        st.info("No regions found. Restore the demo data from Settings.")
        return
    labels = {region.id: f"{region.name} · {region.state.value.replace('_', ' ').title()}"
              for region in regions}
    default_region = st.session_state.get("selected_region")
    if default_region not in labels:
        default_region = next((item.id for item in regions if item.state is RegionState.active), regions[0].id)

    overview, operations, recommendations, activity, settings = st.tabs(
        ["Overview", "Region operations", "Recommendations", "Activity & evidence", "Settings"]
    )
    with overview:
        _render_overview(path, regions)
    with operations:
        _render_region_operations(path, regions, labels, default_region)
    selected_region = st.session_state.get("selected_region", default_region)
    if selected_region not in labels:
        selected_region = default_region
    with recommendations:
        _render_recommendations(path, selected_region)
    with activity:
        _render_activity(path, selected_region)
    with settings:
        _render_settings(path)


def _integration_status(neat_status: str, neat_detail: str) -> None:
    with st.expander("Integration status", expanded=False):
        left, middle, right = st.columns(3)
        left.markdown("**neatlogs**")
        left.caption(f"{neat_status.title()} · {neat_detail}")
        middle.markdown("**cfo.ai**")
        middle.caption("Degraded · Local financial simulation; live scenario read not verified in this session.")
        right.markdown("**Entire**")
        right.caption("Checkpoint evidence is documented; entire-graph is unavailable in this environment.")


def _render_overview(path: Path, regions) -> None:
    active = [item for item in regions if item.state is RegionState.active]
    candidates = [item for item in regions if item.state is RegionState.candidate]
    latest = []
    for region in regions:
        latest.extend(list_region_cycles(path, region.id)[:1])
    latest.sort(key=lambda item: item.created_at, reverse=True)
    last_status = latest[0].status.value if latest else "No cycles yet"
    metric_cols = st.columns(4)
    metric_cols[0].metric("Active regions", len(active))
    metric_cols[1].metric("Awaiting review", len(candidates))
    metric_cols[2].metric("Latest cycle", last_status.replace("_", " ").title())
    metric_cols[3].metric("Products in catalog", len(get_product_catalog(path)))
    st.subheader("Regional portfolio")
    st.caption("Synthetic signal and commerce data · Financial and evaluation results are simulated.")
    rows = [{"Region": item.name, "Status": item.state.value.replace("_", " ").title(),
             "Locale": item.locale} for item in regions]
    st.dataframe(rows, hide_index=True, width="stretch")
    st.subheader("Latest activity")
    if latest:
        for cycle in latest[:4]:
            status = cycle.status.value.title()
            st.markdown(f"**{cycle.region_id}** · {status} · {cycle.created_at.astimezone().strftime('%b %d, %H:%M')} ")
            if cycle.rejection_reason:
                st.caption(cycle.rejection_reason.replace("_", " "))
    else:
        st.info("No autonomous cycles have run. Review a candidate or run a cycle from Region operations.")


def _render_region_operations(path: Path, regions, labels: dict[str, str], default_region: str) -> None:
    st.subheader("Add a candidate region")
    with st.form("candidate"):
        col1, col2 = st.columns([1.2, 1])
        name = col1.text_input("Region name", placeholder="e.g. Harbor Bay")
        monthly_traffic = col2.number_input("Monthly traffic", min_value=0, value=50000, step=1000)
        with st.expander("Financial assumptions", expanded=False):
            a, b, c = st.columns(3)
            conversion = a.number_input("Conversion rate", min_value=0.0, max_value=1.0,
                                        value=0.025, format="%.3f")
            order_value = b.number_input("Average order value", min_value=0.0, value=85.0)
            product_cost = c.number_input("Product cost per order", min_value=0.0, value=45.0)
            d, e, f = st.columns(3)
            fulfillment = d.number_input("Fulfillment per order", min_value=0.0, value=12.0)
            campaign = e.number_input("Monthly campaign spend", min_value=0.0, value=15000.0)
            infrastructure = f.number_input("Monthly infrastructure", min_value=0.0, value=4500.0)
        submitted = st.form_submit_button("Assess candidate", type="primary")
    if submitted:
        try:
            result = submit_candidate(path, CandidateRequest(
                name=name,
                assumptions=FinanceInputs(
                    monthly_traffic=monthly_traffic,
                    conversion_rate=str(conversion),
                    average_order_value=str(order_value),
                    product_cost_per_order=str(product_cost),
                    fulfillment_cost_per_order=str(fulfillment),
                    campaign_cost=str(campaign),
                    infrastructure_cost=str(infrastructure),
                ),
            ))
            st.session_state["selected_region"] = result.region.id
            st.session_state["flash_success"] = "Candidate saved and assessed. It remains inactive until an operator approves it."
            st.rerun()
        except ValidationError:
            st.error("Enter a region name and valid non-negative financial assumptions.")
        except sqlite3.Error:
            st.error("The candidate could not be saved. No partial assessment was committed.")

    st.divider()
    st.subheader("Selected region")
    if st.session_state.get("selected_region") not in labels:
        st.session_state["selected_region"] = default_region
    selected = st.selectbox("Region", options=list(labels), format_func=labels.get,
                            key="selected_region")
    region = next(item for item in regions if item.id == selected)
    report = candidate_report(path, selected)
    export_path = os.environ.get("CFO_SCENARIO_PATH")
    if export_path:
        try:
            imported = read_cfo_export(Path(export_path))
            imported = read_cfo_export(Path(export_path))
            if imported.region_id == selected and persist_cfo_import(path, imported):
                st.warning("Operator-supplied cfo.ai export is attached; live connection and source provenance remain unverified.")
        except (OSError, ValidationError):
            st.error("The configured cfo.ai export could not be read or failed validation. Local simulation remains available.")
    st.caption(f"Lifecycle status · **{region.state.value.replace('_', ' ').title()}**")
    if report:
        _finance_summary(report)
    else:
        st.info("No candidate finance assessment is available for this region.")

    controls = st.columns(5)
    if region.state is RegionState.candidate:
        if controls[0].button("Approve region", key="approve_region", type="primary"):
            _run_operator_action(lambda: approve_region(path, selected), "Region approved and activated.")
        if controls[1].button("Reject", key="reject_region"):
            _run_operator_action(lambda: reject_region(path, selected), "Candidate rejected.")
    elif region.state is RegionState.active:
        if controls[0].button("Run regional cycle", key="run_cycle", type="primary"):
            _run_cycle_action(lambda: run_region_cycle(path, selected))
        if controls[1].button("Pause", key="pause_region"):
            _run_operator_action(lambda: pause_region(path, selected), "Region paused.")
        if controls[2].button("Rollback", key="rollback_region"):
            _run_operator_action(lambda: rollback_region(path, selected), "Previous recommendation version restored.")
        if controls[3].button("Archive", key="archive_region"):
            _run_operator_action(lambda: archive_region(path, selected), "Region archived.")
    elif region.state is RegionState.paused:
        if controls[0].button("Resume", key="resume_region", type="primary"):
            _run_operator_action(lambda: resume_region(path, selected), "Region resumed.")
        if controls[1].button("Archive", key="archive_paused_region"):
            _run_operator_action(lambda: archive_region(path, selected), "Region archived.")

    if region.state is RegionState.active:
        st.markdown("#### Add synthetic evidence")
        with st.form("signal_injection"):
            topics = st.text_input("Topics", value="festival, electronics", help="Comma-separated deterministic topic labels")
            confidence = st.slider("Confidence", min_value=0.0, max_value=1.0, value=0.9, step=0.05)
            evidence = st.text_area("Evidence excerpt", value="Synthetic community signal indicates rising interest in festival and electronics products.")
            add_signal = st.form_submit_button("Add synthetic signal")
        if add_signal:
            try:
                signal = inject_demo_signal(path, selected, [part.strip() for part in topics.split(",") if part.strip()],
                                            confidence, evidence)
                st.success(f"Synthetic signal {signal.id} added to the region inbox.")
            except (ValueError, ValidationError, sqlite3.Error) as error:
                st.error(f"Signal was not added: {error}")
    if controls[4].button("Run all active regions", key="run_all"):
        try:
            results = run_all_active_regions(path)
            for result in results:
                st.write(f"{result.cycle.region_id}: {result.cycle.status.value}")
        except sqlite3.Error:
            st.error("The regional pass could not be persisted.")

    if report and region.state is RegionState.candidate:
        st.caption("The finance result is a recommendation; activation requires the explicit approval action above.")


def _finance_summary(report) -> None:
    st.markdown("#### Financial assessment")
    st.caption(f"Financial model · {report.status.title()} · {report.reason} · Simulated monthly estimates")
    base = report.scenarios[0]
    c1, c2, c3, c4 = st.columns(4)
    c1.metric("Base revenue", f"${base.revenue:,.0f}")
    c2.metric("Contribution profit", f"${base.profit:,.0f}")
    c3.metric("Gross margin", f"{base.gross_margin:.1%}" if base.gross_margin is not None else "—")
    c4.metric("Decision", report.recommendation.title())
    with st.expander("Base, growth, and downside assumptions"):
        st.dataframe([scenario.model_dump(mode="json") for scenario in report.scenarios],
                     hide_index=True, width="stretch")
        st.json(report.assumptions.model_dump(mode="json"))


def _render_recommendations(path: Path, region_id: str) -> None:
    regions = {item.id: item for item in list_regions(path)}
    st.subheader(f"Recommendations · {regions[region_id].name}")
    st.caption("Rankings are deterministic; all sales and evaluation metrics are simulated.")
    ranked = preview_products(path, region_id)
    catalog = get_product_catalog(path)
    if not ranked:
        st.info("This region has no active recommendation profile.")
        return
    current = st.columns(5)
    for column, item in zip(current, ranked[:5]):
        product = catalog[item.product_id]
        with column:
            st.markdown(f"**#{item.rank} · {product.name}**")
            st.caption(f"${product.price:.2f} · {'In stock' if product.in_stock else 'Out of stock'}")
            st.metric("Score", f"{item.score:.2f}")
            with st.expander("Why this product"):
                st.json(item.breakdown.model_dump(mode="json"))
    cycles = list_region_cycles(path, region_id)
    last = next((item for item in cycles if item.evaluation and item.evaluation.get("after")), None)
    if last is None:
        st.info("Run a regional cycle to see a persisted before/after comparison.")
        return
    st.divider()
    st.markdown("#### Latest before / after")
    st.caption(f"Cycle {last.id} · {last.status.value.title()} · {last.rejection_reason or 'Activated'}")
    _render_comparison(last.evaluation.get("before", []), last.evaluation.get("after", []), catalog)
    metrics = last.evaluation
    a, b, c, d = st.columns(4)
    a.metric("Active relevance", f"{metrics.get('active_relevance', 0):.2f}")
    b.metric("Candidate relevance", f"{metrics.get('candidate_relevance', 0):.2f}")
    c.metric("Active simulated profit", f"${metrics.get('active_profit', 0):.2f}")
    d.metric("Candidate simulated profit", f"${metrics.get('candidate_profit', 0):.2f}")


def _render_comparison(before: list[dict], after: list[dict], catalog: dict) -> None:
    before_rank = {item["product_id"]: item for item in before}
    after_rank = {item["product_id"]: item for item in after}
    ids = sorted(set(before_rank) | set(after_rank))
    rows = []
    for product_id in ids:
        old, new = before_rank.get(product_id), after_rank.get(product_id)
        product = catalog.get(product_id)
        rows.append({
            "Product": product.name if product else product_id,
            "Before": old["rank"] if old else "—",
            "After": new["rank"] if new else "—",
            "Movement": (f"↑ {old['rank'] - new['rank']}" if old and new and new["rank"] < old["rank"]
                         else f"↓ {new['rank'] - old['rank']}" if old and new and new["rank"] > old["rank"]
                         else "New" if new and not old else "Removed" if old and not new else "—"),
        })
    st.dataframe(rows, hide_index=True, width="stretch")


def _render_activity(path: Path, region_id: str) -> None:
    st.subheader("Cycle history")
    cycles = list_region_cycles(path, region_id)
    if cycles:
        st.dataframe([{
            "Cycle": item.id,
            "Status": item.status.value.title(),
            "Signals": len(item.signal_ids),
            "Reason": item.rejection_reason or "—",
            "Started": item.created_at.astimezone().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        } for item in cycles], hide_index=True, width="stretch")
        replayable = [item for item in cycles if item.signal_ids]
        if replayable:
            options = {item.id: f"{item.created_at.astimezone().strftime('%b %d %H:%M')} · {item.status.value} · {item.id[:8]}"
                       for item in replayable}
            selected = st.selectbox("Replay source cycle", list(options), format_func=options.get, key="replay_source")
            if st.button("Replay cycle with the same signals", key="replay_cycle"):
                _run_cycle_action(lambda: replay_cycle(path, selected))
    else:
        st.info("No cycles recorded for this region.")
    st.subheader("Operator history")
    actions = list_region_actions(path, region_id)
    if actions:
        st.dataframe([{
            "Action": item["action"].replace("_", " ").title(),
            "When": item["created_at"],
            "Details": str(item["detail"]),
        } for item in actions], hide_index=True, width="stretch")
    else:
        st.caption("Approvals, pauses, resumes, archives, and rollbacks appear here.")


def _render_settings(path: Path) -> None:
    st.subheader("Demo workspace")
    st.caption("Reset restores the checked-in synthetic regions, catalog, signals, and event windows.")
    confirm = st.checkbox("I understand that reset clears local candidates, cycles, and operator history.")
    if st.button("Reset and replay from fixtures", disabled=not confirm, key="reset_demo"):
        try:
            reset_demo(path)
            st.session_state.pop("selected_region", None)
            st.success("Demo state restored from fixtures.")
            st.rerun()
        except sqlite3.Error:
            st.error("Demo state could not be reset.")


def _run_operator_action(action, success_message: str) -> None:
    try:
        result = action()
        st.session_state["flash_success"] = f"{success_message} {result}" if isinstance(result, str) else success_message
        st.rerun()
    except (ValueError, sqlite3.Error) as error:
        st.error(str(error))


def _run_cycle_action(action) -> None:
    try:
        result = action()
        st.session_state["flash_success"] = f"Cycle {result.cycle.status.value}: {result.cycle.id}"
        st.rerun()
    except (ValueError, sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError) as error:
        st.error(f"Cycle did not complete: {error}")

    """Initialize and seed a database without overwriting existing rows."""

        load_fixtures(conn, FIXTURES)

    """Return validated regions in deterministic order."""
    with closing(connect(path)) as conn:
        result = []
        for row in conn.execute("SELECT * FROM regions ORDER BY name"):
            payload = dict(row)

I found why you were seeing repeated rejections. The saved database shows a Cedar cycle that **activated** and changed the active recommendation version. The later Cedar cycles—including the one in your screenshot—were recorded as `no_actionable_signals`: they had no new signal IDs to process. Signals are consumed once, so rerunning without fresh evidence correctly produces no update.

The dashboard made that confusing by showing the no-op as a green success message. I’ve changed it to show pending signal counts, choose an active region with pending evidence by default, explain no-op versus evaluation rejection, and keep the selected dashboard section after an action.

**To see a successful run:**

1. Restart Streamlit so it loads the changes.
2. In **Settings**, confirm and click **Reset and replay from fixtures**. This clears local cycles and restores Cedar’s sample signal.
3. Go to **Region operations**. Cedar Valley should be selected with one new signal waiting.
4. Click **Run regional cycle**. You should see a green “Recommendations updated” message. Check **Recommendations** for the comparison and **Activity & evidence** for the saved cycle.
5. Once that signal is consumed, the run button will be disabled. Add fresh synthetic evidence to run another cycle.

Your existing database was persisting cycles and recommendation versions; the later runs simply had no fresh evidence. The reset clears that state, so it also removes local candidates and operator history.

I verified the fix with **148 passing tests**, plus Python compilation and `git diff --check`. The dashboard tests now cover successful activation, signal consumption, and keeping Region operations selected after the run.

# Plan Mode (Conversational)

You work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.

## Mode rules (strict)

You are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.

Plan Mode is not changed by user intent, tone, or imperative language. If a user asks for execution while still in Plan Mode, treat it as a request to **plan the execution**, not perform it.

## Plan Mode vs update_plan tool

Plan Mode is a collaboration mode that can involve requesting user input and eventually issuing a `<proposed_plan>` block.

Separately, `update_plan` is a checklist/progress/TODOs tool; it does not enter or exit Plan Mode. Do not confuse it with Plan mode or try to use it while in Plan mode. If you try to use `update_plan` in Plan mode, it will return an error.

## Execution vs. mutation in Plan Mode

You may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.

### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)

Actions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs
* Static analysis, inspection, and repo exploration
* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files
* Tests, builds, or checks that may write to caches or build artifacts (for example, `target/`, `.cache/`, or snapshots) so long as they do not edit repo-tracked files

### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)

Actions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Editing or writing files
* Running formatters or linters that rewrite files
* Applying patches, migrations, or codegen that updates repo-tracked files
* Side-effectful commands whose purpose is to carry out the plan rather than refine it

When in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as "doing the work" rather than "planning the work," do not do it.

## PHASE 1 — Ground in the environment (explore first, ask second)

Begin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user. Resolve all questions that can be answered through exploration or inspection. Identify missing or ambiguous details only if they cannot be derived from the environment. Silent exploration between turns is allowed and encouraged.

Before asking the user any question, perform at least one targeted non-mutating exploration pass (for example: search relevant files, inspect likely entrypoints/configs, confirm current implementation shape), unless no local environment/repo is available.

Exception: you may ask clarifying questions about the user's prompt before exploring, ONLY if there are obvious ambiguities or contradictions in the prompt itself. However, if ambiguity might be resolved by exploring, always prefer exploring first.

Do not ask questions that can be answered from the repo or system (for example, "where is this struct?" or "which UI component should we use?" when exploration can make it clear). Only ask once you have exhausted reasonable non-mutating exploration.

## PHASE 2 — Intent chat (what they actually want)

* Keep asking until you can clearly state: goal + success criteria, audience, in/out of scope, constraints, current state, and the key preferences/tradeoffs.
* Bias toward questions over guessing: if any high-impact ambiguity remains, do NOT plan yet—ask.

## PHASE 3 — Implementation chat (what/how we’ll build)

* Once intent is stable, keep asking until the spec is decision complete: approach, interfaces (APIs/schemas/I/O), data flow, edge cases/failure modes, testing + acceptance criteria, rollout/monitoring, and any migrations/compat constraints.

## Asking questions

Critical rules:

* Strongly prefer using the `request_user_input` tool to ask any questions.
* Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.
* In rare cases where an unavoidable, important question can’t be expressed with reasonable multiple‑choice options (due to extreme ambiguity), you may ask it directly without the tool.

You SHOULD ask many questions, but each question must:

* materially change the spec/plan, OR
* confirm/lock an assumption, OR
* choose between meaningful tradeoffs.
* not be answerable by non-mutating commands.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for decisions that materially change the plan, for confirming important assumptions, or for information that cannot be discovered via non-mutating exploration.

## Two kinds of unknowns (treat differently)

1. **Discoverable facts** (repo/system truth): explore first.

   * Before asking, run targeted searches and check likely sources of truth (configs/manifests/entrypoints/schemas/types/constants).
   * Ask only if: multiple plausible candidates; nothing found but you need a missing identifier/context; or ambiguity is actually product intent.
   * If asking, present concrete candidates (paths/service names) + recommend one.
   * Never ask questions you can answer from your environment (e.g., “where is this struct”).

2. **Preferences/tradeoffs** (not discoverable): ask early.

   * These are intent or implementation preferences that cannot be derived from exploration.
   * Provide 2–4 mutually exclusive options + a recommended default.
   * If unanswered, proceed with the recommended option and record it as an assumption in the final plan.

## Finalization rule

Only output the final plan when it is decision complete and leaves no decisions to the implementer.

When you present the official plan, wrap it in a `<proposed_plan>` block so the client can render it specially:

1) The opening tag must be on its own line.
2) Start the plan content on the next line (no text on the same line as the tag).
3) The closing tag must be on its own line.
4) Use Markdown inside the block.
5) Keep the tags exactly as `<proposed_plan>` and `</proposed_plan>` (do not translate or rename them), even if the plan content is in another language.

Example:

<proposed_plan>
plan content
</proposed_plan>

plan content should be human and agent digestible. The final plan must be plan-only, concise by default, and include:

* A clear title
* A brief summary section
* Important changes or additions to public APIs/interfaces/types
* Test cases and scenarios
* Explicit assumptions and defaults chosen where needed

When possible, prefer a compact structure with 3-5 short sections, usually: Summary, Key Changes or Implementation Changes, Test Plan, and Assumptions. Do not include a separate Scope section unless scope boundaries are genuinely important to avoid mistakes.

Prefer grouped implementation bullets by subsystem or behavior over file-by-file inventories. Mention files only when needed to disambiguate a non-obvious change, and avoid naming more than 3 paths unless extra specificity is necessary to prevent mistakes. Prefer behavior-level descriptions over symbol-by-symbol removal lists. For v1 feature-addition plans, do not invent detailed schema, validation, precedence, fallback, or wire-shape policy unless the request establishes it or it is needed to prevent a concrete implementation mistake; prefer the intended capability and minimum interface/behavior changes.

Keep bullets short and avoid explanatory sub-bullets unless they are needed to prevent ambiguity. Prefer the minimum detail needed for implementation safety, not exhaustive coverage. Within each section, compress related changes into a few high-signal bullets and omit branch-by-branch logic, repeated invariants, and long lists of unaffected behavior unless they are necessary to prevent a likely implementation mistake. Avoid repeated repo facts and irrelevant edge-case or rollout detail. For straightforward refactors, keep the plan to a compact summary, key edits, tests, and assumptions. If the user asks for more detail, then expand.

Do not ask "should I proceed?" in the final output. The user can easily switch out of Plan mode and request implementation if you have included a `<proposed_plan>` block in your response. Alternatively, they can decide to stay in Plan mode and continue refining the plan.

Only produce at most one `<proposed_plan>` block per turn, and only when you are presenting a complete spec.

If the user stays in Plan mode and asks for revisions after a prior `<proposed_plan>`, any new `<proposed_plan>` must be a complete replacement. If the user indicates that the prior plan is not acceptable but does not provide enough information to produce a complete replacement, address the concern and continue planning without producing a `<proposed_plan>` block. If the follow-up neither requires changes nor calls the plan into question (e.g. clarifying question), answer it before the block, then reproduce the prior `<proposed_plan>` unchanged.

Use **Aspen Ridge** and the topic **`festival`**. Aspen has no seeded signal, so the experiment starts from a clean profile. Signals are processed once, so reset before each trial.

### Trial 1: confidence 0.70

1. In **Settings**, reset the demo.
2. Go to **Region operations** and select **Aspen Ridge**.
3. Under **Add synthetic evidence**, enter topic `festival`, set confidence to **0.70**, and keep the sample evidence text.
4. Click **Add synthetic signal**, then **Run regional cycle**.
5. Open **Recommendations** for Aspen Ridge. The cycle should activate; festival products should move into the rankings.

### Trial 2: confidence 0.80

Reset and repeat with confidence **0.80**. The proposal should give festival products a stronger boost, but the simulated profit guardrail is expected to reject this update. In **Recommendations**, compare the proposed before/after rankings; the active recommendations should stay unchanged because the proposal was rejected.

For a confidence-gate check, repeat once more at **0.65**. That signal is below the app’s **0.70 minimum**, so it should produce no update. The cycle details should show `low_confidence`.

Compare the cycle details as well as the product list: confidence changes the proposed topic weight, but the quality and profit checks determine whether that proposal becomes active.

settings.developer_instructions:
# Plan Mode (Conversational)

You work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.

## Mode rules (strict)

You are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.

Plan Mode is not changed by user intent, tone, or imperative language. If a user asks for execution while still in Plan Mode, treat it as a request to **plan the execution**, not perform it.

## Plan Mode vs update_plan tool

Plan Mode is a collaboration mode that can involve requesting user input and eventually issuing a `<proposed_plan>` block.

Separately, `update_plan` is a checklist/progress/TODOs tool; it does not enter or exit Plan Mode. Do not confuse it with Plan mode or try to use it while in Plan mode. If you try to use `update_plan` in Plan mode, it will return an error.

## Execution vs. mutation in Plan Mode

You may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.

### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)

Actions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs
* Static analysis, inspection, and repo exploration
* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files
* Tests, builds, or checks that may write to caches or build artifacts (for example, `target/`, `.cache/`, or snapshots) so long as they do not edit repo-tracked files

### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)

Actions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Editing or writing files
* Running formatters or linters that rewrite files
* Applying patches, migrations, or codegen that updates repo-tracked files
* Side-effectful commands whose purpose is to carry out the plan rather than refine it

When in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as "doing the work" rather than "planning the work," do not do it.

## PHASE 1 — Ground in the environment (explore first, ask second)

Begin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user. Resolve all questions that can be answered through exploration or inspection. Identify missing or ambiguous details only if they cannot be derived from the environment. Silent exploration between turns is allowed and encouraged.

Before asking the user any question, perform at least one targeted non-mutating exploration pass (for example: search relevant files, inspect likely entrypoints/configs, confirm current implementation shape), unless no local environment/repo is available.

Exception: you may ask clarifying questions about the user's prompt before exploring, ONLY if there are obvious ambiguities or contradictions in the prompt itself. However, if ambiguity might be resolved by exploring, always prefer exploring first.

Do not ask questions that can be answered from the repo or system (for example, "where is this struct?" or "which UI component should we use?" when exploration can make it clear). Only ask once you have exhausted reasonable non-mutating exploration.

## PHASE 2 — Intent chat (what they actually want)

* Keep asking until you can clearly state: goal + success criteria, audience, in/out of scope, constraints, current state, and the key preferences/tradeoffs.
* Bias toward questions over guessing: if any high-impact ambiguity remains, do NOT plan yet—ask.

## PHASE 3 — Implementation chat (what/how we’ll build)

* Once intent is stable, keep asking until the spec is decision complete: approach, interfaces (APIs/schemas/I/O), data flow, edge cases/failure modes, testing + acceptance criteria, rollout/monitoring, and any migrations/compat constraints.

## Asking questions

Critical rules:

* Strongly prefer using the `request_user_input` tool to ask any questions.
* Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.
* In rare cases where an unavoidable, important question can’t be expressed with reasonable multiple‑choice options (due to extreme ambiguity), you may ask it directly without the tool.

You SHOULD ask many questions, but each question must:

* materially change the spec/plan, OR
* confirm/lock an assumption, OR
* choose between meaningful tradeoffs.
* not be answerable by non-mutating commands.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for decisions that materially change the plan, for confirming important assumptions, or for information that cannot be discovered via non-mutating exploration.

## Two kinds of unknowns (treat differently)

1. **Discoverable facts** (repo/system truth): explore first.

   * Before asking, run targeted searches and check likely sources of truth (configs/manifests/entrypoints/schemas/types/constants).
   * Ask only if: multiple plausible candidates; nothing found but you need a missing identifier/context; or ambiguity is actually product intent.
   * If asking, present concrete candidates (paths/service names) + recommend one.
   * Never ask questions you can answer from your environment (e.g., “where is this struct”).

2. **Preferences/tradeoffs** (not discoverable): ask early.

   * These are intent or implementation preferences that cannot be derived from exploration.
   * Provide 2–4 mutually exclusive options + a recommended default.
   * If unanswered, proceed with the recommended option and record it as an assumption in the final plan.

## Finalization rule

Only output the final plan when it is decision complete and leaves no decisions to the implementer.

When you present the official plan, wrap it in a `<proposed_plan>` block so the client can render it specially:

1) The opening tag must be on its own line.
2) Start the plan content on the next line (no text on the same line as the tag).
3) The closing tag must be on its own line.
4) Use Markdown inside the block.
5) Keep the tags exactly as `<proposed_plan>` and `</proposed_plan>` (do not translate or rename them), even if the plan content is in another language.

Example:

<proposed_plan>
plan content
</proposed_plan>

plan content should be human and agent digestible. The final plan must be plan-only, concise by default, and include:

* A clear title
* A brief summary section
* Important changes or additions to public APIs/interfaces/types
* Test cases and scenarios
* Explicit assumptions and defaults chosen where needed

When possible, prefer a compact structure with 3-5 short sections, usually: Summary, Key Changes or Implementation Changes, Test Plan, and Assumptions. Do not include a separate Scope section unless scope boundaries are genuinely important to avoid mistakes.

Prefer grouped implementation bullets by subsystem or behavior over file-by-file inventories. Mention files only when needed to disambiguate a non-obvious change, and avoid naming more than 3 paths unless extra specificity is necessary to prevent mistakes. Prefer behavior-level descriptions over symbol-by-symbol removal lists. For v1 feature-addition plans, do not invent detailed schema, validation, precedence, fallback, or wire-shape policy unless the request establishes it or it is needed to prevent a concrete implementation mistake; prefer the intended capability and minimum interface/behavior changes.

Keep bullets short and avoid explanatory sub-bullets unless they are needed to prevent ambiguity. Prefer the minimum detail needed for implementation safety, not exhaustive coverage. Within each section, compress related changes into a few high-signal bullets and omit branch-by-branch logic, repeated invariants, and long lists of unaffected behavior unless they are necessary to prevent a likely implementation mistake. Avoid repeated repo facts and irrelevant edge-case or rollout detail. For straightforward refactors, keep the plan to a compact summary, key edits, tests, and assumptions. If the user asks for more detail, then expand.

Do not ask "should I proceed?" in the final output. The user can easily switch out of Plan mode and request implementation if you have included a `<proposed_plan>` block in your response. Alternatively, they can decide to stay in Plan mode and continue refining the plan.

Only produce at most one `<proposed_plan>` block per turn, and only when you are presenting a complete spec.

If the user stays in Plan mode and asks for revisions after a prior `<proposed_plan>`, any new `<proposed_plan>` must be a complete replacement. If the user indicates that the prior plan is not acceptable but does not provide enough information to produce a complete replacement, address the concern and continue planning without producing a `<proposed_plan>` block. If the follow-up neither requires changes nor calls the plan into question (e.g. clarifying question), answer it before the block, then reproduce the prior `<proposed_plan>` unchanged.

"""Operator utilities for synthetic evidence and a repeatable demo reset."""

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4

from adaptive_commerce.domain import Signal, SignalSourceType
from adaptive_commerce.persistence import Repository, connect, load_fixtures

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "data" / "fixtures"


def inject_demo_signal(
    path: Path,
    region_id: str,
    topics: list[str],
    confidence: float,
    evidence: str,
    source_type: SignalSourceType = SignalSourceType.social,
    observed_at: datetime | None = None,
) -> Signal:
    """Persist an explicitly synthetic signal for an operator demonstration."""
    with connect(path) as conn:
        repository = Repository(conn)
        region = repository.get_region(region_id)
        if region is None:
            raise ValueError("selected region does not exist")
        signal = Signal(
            id=f"signal:{uuid4().hex}",
            region_id=region_id,
            source_id=f"demo:{uuid4().hex}",
            source_type=source_type,
            topics=topics,
            confidence=confidence,
            observed_at=observed_at or datetime.now(timezone.utc),
            evidence_excerpt=evidence,
            language="en",
            normalized_text=evidence,
        )
        repository.create_signal(signal)
        return signal


def reset_demo(path: Path) -> None:
    """Clear local application state and restore the checked-in synthetic fixtures."""
    with connect(path) as conn:
        conn.execute("PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = ON")
        for table in (
            "evidence_references", "recommendation_items", "consumed_signals", "signals", "source_records",
            "event_windows", "finance_assessments", "operator_actions", "update_cycles",
            "simulated_events", "region_profiles", "recommendation_versions", "regions",
            "products",
        ):
            conn.execute(f"DELETE FROM {table}")
        load_fixtures(conn, FIXTURES)
    assert result.metrics["min_profit_retention"] == "0.99"
    assert result.after_version_id == result.before_version_id


def test_low_confidence_is_rejected_and_consumed_once(demo_db):
    inject_demo_signal(
        demo_db, "aspen", ["festival", "electronics"], 0.2,
        "Synthetic low-confidence signal for the recovery acceptance scenario.",
    )
    result = run_region_cycle(demo_db, "aspen", now=NOW)
    assert result.cycle.status is UpdateCycleStatus.rejected
    assert result.cycle.rejection_reason == "no_actionable_signals"
    assert result.metrics["rejections"][0]["reason"] == "low_confidence"
    next_cycle = run_region_cycle(demo_db, "aspen", now=NOW)
    assert next_cycle.cycle.status is UpdateCycleStatus.rejected
    assert next_cycle.cycle.signal_ids == []


def test_pause_excludes_region_and_scheduler_isolates_regions(demo_db, monkeypatch):
    pause_region(demo_db, "aspen")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="active region"):
        run_region_cycle(demo_db, "aspen", now=NOW)
    resume_region(demo_db, "aspen")
    results = run_all_active_regions(demo_db, now=NOW, max_attempts=1)
    assert {item.cycle.region_id for item in results} == {"cedar", "aspen"}


def test_failed_region_does_not_stop_other_region(demo_db, monkeypatch):
    import adaptive_commerce.application.worker as worker_module

    real_run = worker_module.run_region_cycle

    def fail_cedar(path, region_id, **kwargs):
        if region_id == "cedar":
            raise RuntimeError("injected local failure")
        return real_run(path, region_id, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(worker_module, "run_region_cycle", fail_cedar)
    results = worker_module.run_all_active_regions(demo_db, now=NOW, max_attempts=1)
    by_region = {item.cycle.region_id: item.cycle for item in results}
    assert by_region["cedar"].status is UpdateCycleStatus.failed
    assert by_region["aspen"].status is UpdateCycleStatus.rejected


def test_replay_uses_same_signals_as_new_cycle_and_reset_restores_fixtures(demo_db):
    result = run_region_cycle(demo_db, "cedar", now=NOW, cycle_id="cycle-to-replay")
    replay = replay_cycle(demo_db, result.cycle.id, now=NOW)
    assert replay.cycle.id != result.cycle.id
    assert replay.cycle.signal_ids == result.cycle.signal_ids
    assert replay.replay_of == result.cycle.id
    reset_demo(demo_db)
    with connect(demo_db) as conn:
        assert Repository(conn).get_update_cycle(result.cycle.id) is None
        assert Repository(conn).get_region("cedar").state is RegionState.active
    assert len(list_regions(demo_db)) == 3

"""Validated, deterministic extraction from synthetic source records."""

import logging
import re
from datetime import datetime
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Annotated, Any, Mapping, Sequence

from pydantic import AwareDatetime, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator

from adaptive_commerce.domain import EventWindow, Signal, SignalSourceType
from adaptive_commerce.integrations.observability import traced_step

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

Identifier = Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)]
FiniteDecimal = Annotated[Decimal, Field(allow_inf_nan=False)]
Impact = Annotated[FiniteDecimal, Field(ge=-1, le=1)]


class SignalBoundaryModel(BaseModel):
    """Strict model used at the synthetic source and agent boundary."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", str_strip_whitespace=True)


class FixtureEvent(SignalBoundaryModel):
    """Optional event timing attached to a synthetic source record."""

    id: Identifier
    starts_at: AwareDatetime
    expires_at: AwareDatetime

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_window(self) -> "FixtureEvent":
        """Require a non-empty half-open event interval."""
        if self.expires_at <= self.starts_at:
            raise ValueError("expires_at must be after starts_at")
        return self


class FixtureSourceRecord(SignalBoundaryModel):
    """Synthetic source input with explicit extraction labels.

    The fixture supplies topics, confidence, and direction so tests and demos do
    not depend on an LLM. A later extractor can construct this same boundary.
    """

    id: Identifier
    region_id: Identifier
    source_type: SignalSourceType
    observed_at: AwareDatetime
    content: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=20_000)
    topics: list[Identifier] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=20)
    confidence: Annotated[FiniteDecimal, Field(ge=0, le=1)]
    topic_impacts: dict[Identifier, Impact] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    language: str = Field(default="en", min_length=2, max_length=35)
    event: FixtureEvent | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_labels(self) -> "FixtureSourceRecord":
        """Reject ambiguous labels and event metadata on non-event records."""
        normalized_topics = [_normalize_topic(topic) for topic in self.topics]
        if len(set(normalized_topics)) != len(normalized_topics):
            raise ValueError("topics must be unique after normalization")
        unknown_impacts = set(self.topic_impacts) - set(self.topics)
        if unknown_impacts:
            raise ValueError("topic_impacts keys must appear in topics")
        if self.event is not None and self.source_type is not SignalSourceType.event:
            raise ValueError("event metadata requires source_type='event'")
        return self


class NormalizedSignal(SignalBoundaryModel):
    """Shared signal plus Ad-owned directional and temporary-event metadata."""

    signal: Signal
    topic_impacts: dict[Identifier, Impact]
    event: FixtureEvent | None = None

content.text:
I found why your confidence test kept declining. The cycle in the database contained **two identical Aspen signals at 0.80 confidence**. Together they hit the region’s maximum topic-weight change, so the proposed ranking shifted sharply and simulated profit fell below the guardrail. The app correctly kept the active recommendations unchanged, but it made it too easy to submit the same synthetic signal more than once.

I’ve made the confidence demo easier to test:

- Repeated identical synthetic submissions now reuse one signal record. To represent a separate observation, change the evidence text.
- The signal form now defaults to `festival` at `0.70` and shows how confidence scales the proposed topic change.
- Rejection messages state the profit threshold, and the cycle tests cover `0.65`, `0.70`, and `0.80`.

**Try it again:** restart Streamlit, reset in **Settings** to clear the old signals, select **Aspen Ridge**, and submit the default festival signal **once**. At `0.70`, the test-calibrated result should activate and bring LED String Lights into Aspen’s top five. Reset before each comparison: `0.65` should fail the confidence gate, while `0.80` may propose a larger change that the profit guardrail rejects. For a rejected proposal, **Latest before / after** shows the candidate ranking; the active list remains unchanged.

This keeps the future LLM seam clean: the LLM can produce a validated signal with topics and confidence, while deterministic ranking and evaluation decide whether to activate it. The LLM itself does not set product ranks.

You work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.

## Mode rules (strict)

You are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.

Plan Mode is not changed by user intent, tone, or imperative language. If a user asks for execution while still in Plan Mode, treat it as a request to **plan the execution**, not perform it.

## Plan Mode vs update_plan tool

Plan Mode is a collaboration mode that can involve requesting user input and eventually issuing a `<proposed_plan>` block.

Separately, `update_plan` is a checklist/progress/TODOs tool; it does not enter or exit Plan Mode. Do not confuse it with Plan mode or try to use it while in Plan mode. If you try to use `update_plan` in Plan mode, it will return an error.

## Execution vs. mutation in Plan Mode

You may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.

### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)

Actions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs
* Static analysis, inspection, and repo exploration
* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files
* Tests, builds, or checks that may write to caches or build artifacts (for example, `target/`, `.cache/`, or snapshots) so long as they do not edit repo-tracked files

### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)

Actions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Editing or writing files
* Running formatters or linters that rewrite files
* Applying patches, migrations, or codegen that updates repo-tracked files
* Side-effectful commands whose purpose is to carry out the plan rather than refine it

When in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as "doing the work" rather than "planning the work," do not do it.

## PHASE 1 — Ground in the environment (explore first, ask second)

Begin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user. Resolve all questions that can be answered through exploration or inspection. Identify missing or ambiguous details only if they cannot be derived from the environment. Silent exploration between turns is allowed and encouraged.

Before asking the user any question, perform at least one targeted non-mutating exploration pass (for example: search relevant files, inspect likely entrypoints/configs, confirm current implementation shape), unless no local environment/repo is available.

Exception: you may ask clarifying questions about the user's prompt before exploring, ONLY if there are obvious ambiguities or contradictions in the prompt itself. However, if ambiguity might be resolved by exploring, always prefer exploring first.

Do not ask questions that can be answered from the repo or system (for example, "where is this struct?" or "which UI component should we use?" when exploration can make it clear). Only ask once you have exhausted reasonable non-mutating exploration.

## PHASE 2 — Intent chat (what they actually want)

* Keep asking until you can clearly state: goal + success criteria, audience, in/out of scope, constraints, current state, and the key preferences/tradeoffs.
* Bias toward questions over guessing: if any high-impact ambiguity remains, do NOT plan yet—ask.

## PHASE 3 — Implementation chat (what/how we’ll build)

* Once intent is stable, keep asking until the spec is decision complete: approach, interfaces (APIs/schemas/I/O), data flow, edge cases/failure modes, testing + acceptance criteria, rollout/monitoring, and any migrations/compat constraints.

## Asking questions

Critical rules:

* Strongly prefer using the `request_user_input` tool to ask any questions.
* Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.
* In rare cases where an unavoidable, important question can’t be expressed with reasonable multiple‑choice options (due to extreme ambiguity), you may ask it directly without the tool.

You SHOULD ask many questions, but each question must:

* materially change the spec/plan, OR
* confirm/lock an assumption, OR
* choose between meaningful tradeoffs.
* not be answerable by non-mutating commands.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for decisions that materially change the plan, for confirming important assumptions, or for information that cannot be discovered via non-mutating exploration.

1. **Discoverable facts** (repo/system truth): explore first.

   * Before asking, run targeted searches and check likely sources of truth (configs/manifests/entrypoints/schemas/types/constants).
   * Ask only if: multiple plausible candidates; nothing found but you need a missing identifier/context; or ambiguity is actually product intent.
   * If asking, present concrete candidates (paths/service names) + recommend one.
   * Never ask questions you can answer from your environment (e.g., “where is this struct”).

2. **Preferences/tradeoffs** (not discoverable): ask early.

   * These are intent or implementation preferences that cannot be derived from exploration.
   * Provide 2–4 mutually exclusive options + a recommended default.
   * If unanswered, proceed with the recommended option and record it as an assumption in the final plan.

1) The opening tag must be on its own line.
2) Start the plan content on the next line (no text on the same line as the tag).
3) The closing tag must be on its own line.
4) Use Markdown inside the block.
5) Keep the tags exactly as `<proposed_plan>` and `</proposed_plan>` (do not translate or rename them), even if the plan content is in another language.

Example:

<proposed_plan>
plan content
</proposed_plan>

plan content should be human and agent digestible. The final plan must be plan-only, concise by default, and include:

* A clear title
* A brief summary section
* Important changes or additions to public APIs/interfaces/types
* Test cases and scenarios
* Explicit assumptions and defaults chosen where needed

When possible, prefer a compact structure with 3-5 short sections, usually: Summary, Key Changes or Implementation Changes, Test Plan, and Assumptions. Do not include a separate Scope section unless scope boundaries are genuinely important to avoid mistakes.

Prefer grouped implementation bullets by subsystem or behavior over file-by-file inventories. Mention files only when needed to disambiguate a non-obvious change, and avoid naming more than 3 paths unless extra specificity is necessary to prevent mistakes. Prefer behavior-level descriptions over symbol-by-symbol removal lists. For v1 feature-addition plans, do not invent detailed schema, validation, precedence, fallback, or wire-shape policy unless the request establishes it or it is needed to prevent a concrete implementation mistake; prefer the intended capability and minimum interface/behavior changes.

Keep bullets short and avoid explanatory sub-bullets unless they are needed to prevent ambiguity. Prefer the minimum detail needed for implementation safety, not exhaustive coverage. Within each section, compress related changes into a few high-signal bullets and omit branch-by-branch logic, repeated invariants, and long lists of unaffected behavior unless they are necessary to prevent a likely implementation mistake. Avoid repeated repo facts and irrelevant edge-case or rollout detail. For straightforward refactors, keep the plan to a compact summary, key edits, tests, and assumptions. If the user asks for more detail, then expand.

Do not ask "should I proceed?" in the final output. The user can easily switch out of Plan mode and request implementation if you have included a `<proposed_plan>` block in your response. Alternatively, they can decide to stay in Plan mode and continue refining the plan.

If the user indicates that the prior plan is not acceptable but does not provide enough information to produce a complete replacement, address the concern and continue planning without producing a `<proposed_plan>` block. If the follow-up neither requires changes nor calls the plan into question (e.g. clarifying question), answer it before the block, then reproduce the prior `<proposed_plan>` unchanged.

"""Initialize the official neatlogs SDK once; never claim unverified export."""

import logging
import os
from contextlib import contextmanager
from functools import lru_cache, wraps
from inspect import signature
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator, TypeVar

import neatlogs
from pydantic import BaseModel

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
F = TypeVar("F", bound=Callable[..., Any])


class TraceStatus(BaseModel):
    """Runtime configuration status, separate from live trace readback evidence."""

    status: str
    detail: str


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def initialize_tracing() -> TraceStatus:
    """Configure one SDK generation with export disabled when no key exists."""
    key = os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY")
    try:
        neatlogs.init(
            api_key=key, workflow_name="atlas-commerce",
            disable_export=not bool(key), capture_logs=False,
        )
    except Exception:
        logger.error("neatlogs_initialization_failed")
        return TraceStatus(status="failed", detail="neatlogs initialization failed; see local diagnostics.")
    if not key:
        return TraceStatus(status="degraded", detail="NEATLOGS_API_KEY missing; local spans only, no live export.")
    return TraceStatus(status="configured", detail="Export configured; live trace readback still requires verification.")


@contextmanager
def trace_step(
    kind: str,
    name: str,
    *,
    region_id: str | None = None,
    cycle_id: str | None = None,
    version_id: str | None = None,
) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Create a content-free Neatlogs span with Atlas workflow identifiers."""
    with neatlogs.trace(name, kind=kind) as span:
        for key, value in (
            ("region_id", region_id),
            ("cycle_id", cycle_id),
            ("version_id", version_id),
        ):
            if value is not None:
                span.set_attribute(f"atlas.{key}", value)
        yield


def traced_step(
    kind: str,
    name: str,
    attributes: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str | None]],
) -> Callable[[F], F]:
    """Decorate a service step and derive safe span IDs from its arguments."""
    def decorate(function: F) -> F:
        parameters = signature(function)

        @wraps(function)
        def wrapped(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
            bound = parameters.bind_partial(*args, **kwargs)
            with trace_step(kind, name, **attributes(bound.arguments)):
                return function(*args, **kwargs)

        return wrapped  # type: ignore[return-value]

    return decorate
